evals.prompt: Can you review MR !42 in my project? I want to make sure there aren't any bugs before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: The skill should fetch MR !42's metadata, materialize its head in an isolated git worktree, analyze the local changes for bugs and issues, and post a signed review comment to the MR.
expectations: Uses glab mr view to fetch MR metadata
Fetches the MR head and target branch as temporary Git refs
Creates a detached temporary git worktree without switching the user's checkout
Uses a local merge-base and git diff to identify the MR changes
Does not use glab mr diff or the MR changes API
Posts review comments using glab api with body=@file pattern
Every comment ends with a signature block containing tool and model name
Provides a summary note at the end
Removes the temporary worktree and refs after the review

evals.prompt: Check the test coverage on MR !17 — I added a new auth module and want to know if the tests are thorough enough.
evals.expected_output: The skill should materialize MR !17 in a temporary worktree and focus on test coverage analysis for the auth module changes, identifying gaps and rating their importance.
expectations: Creates an isolated worktree at the fetched MR head
Uses local git diff output to scope the changed auth code and tests
Runs repository inspection or tests from the temporary worktree
Does not use glab mr diff or the MR changes API
Focuses review on test-related aspects (tests aspect)
Identifies critical test gaps and rates them
Posts signed review comments
Does not review non-test code unless it affects testability

evals.prompt: Do a comprehensive review of MR !8 — check code quality, error handling, and suggest any simplifications. I want this to be thorough.
evals.expected_output: The skill should perform a multi-aspect review covering code, errors, and simplification, posting individual findings and a comprehensive summary.
expectations: Reviews multiple aspects: code, errors, simplify
Posts individual findings for each issue found
Posts a comprehensive summary note categorizing issues by severity
Uses confidence scoring for code issues
Signature block present on all comments
Summary categorizes into Critical/Important/Suggestions/Positive

evals.prompt: Review MR !31 — it's a Python service, just check the code quality.
evals.expected_output: The skill should load house-rules.md and python.md, flag any unjustified noqa/type:ignore/pylint-disable suppressions (confidence 80-90), and post signed inline comments including the rule rationale. Justified suppressions at a verified boundary with a guard and stated reason should not be flagged.
expectations: Loads references/house-rules.md and references/python.md before analysis
Flags lint/type suppressions lacking both a runtime guard and a stated reason
Does not flag suppressions at a verified boundary that have a guard and a reason
Posts signed inline comments that include the rule rationale
Uses confidence scoring 80-90 for these findings

evals.prompt: Do a code review of MR !55 — it's a TypeScript frontend that calls a new backend endpoint.
evals.expected_output: The skill should load house-rules.md and typescript.md, flag unvalidated JSON.parse/response.json results and unvalidated shared state (confidence 80-90), and post signed inline comments. Internally-constructed data with known shape should not be flagged.
expectations: Loads references/house-rules.md and references/typescript.md before analysis
Flags response.json()/JSON.parse results used without a zod schema parse
Flags unvalidated state objects passed to multiple functions
Does not flag internally-constructed data with known shape
Posts signed inline comments that include the rule rationale

evals.prompt: Review MR !73, but I have uncommitted work in my current checkout, so don't disturb it.
evals.expected_output: The skill should preserve the user's current checkout, fetch MR !73 into private temporary refs, review it from a detached temporary worktree, and clean up only the resources it created.
expectations: Does not checkout, reset, stash, or modify the user's current worktree
Fetches refs/merge-requests/73/head and the target branch into private temporary refs
Creates a detached temporary worktree at the MR head
Computes the comparison base locally with git merge-base
Reads files and runs checks from the temporary worktree
Does not use glab mr diff or the MR changes API
Removes only the temporary worktree and refs created for the review
